Method of Attack: Using malicious Microsoft OneNote '.one' attachments containing embedded HTML application (HTA) files that retrieve and execute QBot malware payload
Embedding VBS or LNK files in OneNote documents executed by user double-click
Hijacking existing email threads to send malicious OneNote Notebook files as reply-to-all attachments
Using social engineering with fake buttons to trick users into launching embedded attachments
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious OneNote '.one' attachments
Thread injection in email replies with malicious OneNote attachments
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious OneNote '.one' files with embedded HTA files
Use of legitimate curl.exe to download DLL payload to C:\ProgramData
Injection into Windows Assistive Technology manager process (AtBroker.exe)
